capabilities: Sync notes and attachments across devices over WebSockets
Encrypt file contents, paths, and attachments locally with AES-256-GCM before upload
Self-host the backend on a VPS via Docker or serverless on Cloudflare Workers
Upload only changed blocks using content-addressed chunk deduplication
Queue edits offline in an IndexedDB outbox and retry with exponential backoff
extras: Deployment guides for the required server live in a separate Onyx main repository linked from the README; the README also includes a Chinese-language summary. The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
motivation: The README frames the goal as giving users full ownership over their notes with client-side encryption, so the server stores only ciphertext and hashes.
problem: Syncing a vault usually means trusting a server operator with plaintext content; users who want to keep notes private even from the server admin have no built-in option.

requires.name: Onyx backend server (Docker/VPS or Cloudflare Workers deployment)

summary: Self-hosted zero-knowledge sync engine that end-to-end encrypts notes and attachments before they reach your own VPS or Cloudflare Workers server.
